fatal_errors: The proposed single-phase high-entropy diboride is fundamentally different from the target intervention: a ZrB2 cermet containing 30% AlFeNiCoCr high-entropy-alloy binder.

The hypothesis misses the 1500 °C SPS optimum and the liquid-binder pore-filling mechanism; it instead proposes approximately 1700 °C processing and an unsupported configurational-entropy densification mechanism.
None of the cited evidence establishes resistance to prolonged molten-aluminum or plating-metal corrosion.
The liquid-metal experiment lacks a specified bath composition, temperature, exposure duration, quantitative corrosion-rate measurement, and the relevant 1300–1600 °C processing controls.
explanation: The response recognizes the combined low-temperature processing, mechanical, oxidation, and liquid-metal durability problem and offers a testable alternative. Its citations validly support formation of some single-phase high-entropy diborides, the approximate size-mismatch phase boundary, and comparative hardness and oxidation behavior. However, they do not support the claimed liquid-metal corrosion benefit or show that configurational entropy lowers the densification barrier. The reconstruction misses the target composition, 30% AlFeNiCoCr binder, 1500 °C SPS condition, binder-flow densification mechanism, 1600 °C binder-loss failure boundary, and quantitative density, toughness, wear, and molten-Al corrosion outcomes. The proposed experiment has useful phase, microstructure, hardness, oxidation, and corrosion categories, but it is insufficiently specified to evaluate prolonged molten-Al service or distinguish the target processing optimum.
